subject: Phased egress credit + tiered seat bundling for Vertex Systems
messages:
From: Alex Caldwell <alex.caldwell@vertexsys.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@vertexsys.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring price parity + migration credits

Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers on your Dedicated profile. Procurement asked me to surface two practical items before we move forward: 1) whether you can offer an 'egress' credit to offset outbound data while we migrate models/data, and 2) if there's a way to structure seats/bundles so our teams can ramp without over-committing up-front.

High-level target: a 12-month committed plan with a 3-month phased migration (pilot -> staged production) and a predictable blended rate. Can you put together a proposal showing a phased credit structure (e.g., month 1-3 heavier credit, tapering thereafter) and a seat-based bundle so we can add seats in month 4/7/10? Also flag any procurement/legal must-haves (data locality/SLA).

Cheers,
Alex
VP Cloud Architecture
Vertex Systems
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Caldwell <alex.caldwell@vertexsys.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring price parity + migration credits

Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks. I attached a short proposal that lays out:
- A phased egress credit (90% month 1, 60% month 2, 30% month 3) applied to outbound transfer charges tied to migration windows.
- A tiered seat bundle (Starter / Growth / Scale) where you pre-purchase a base seat count and purchase additional delta seats at a discounted pass-through price at the quarter boundaries you mentioned.
- A one-time migration services credit (applied to Professional Services hours) to cover onboarding and split-testing the KV-cache for hot prompts.

Two quick notes:
1) The egress credit is operationally gated — credits apply if we run migration traffic through designated IP ranges so we can attribute transfer. If Vertex needs custom networking (carrier/MPLS) we should discuss separately.
2) We can do a 6% one-time signing credit if you commit to 12 months now; otherwise the phased credit schedule above is the conservative path.

I've looped Marissa and Markus for pricing authorization and legal redline coordination. If that model looks reasonable I'll push a clean proposal and redline document for procurement.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270422_vertex-proposal-v1.pdf
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-23T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring price parity + migration credits

Kim —

Pricing guidance: I'm comfortable with the proposed taper (90/60/30) as a short-term migration allowance if we require that migration egress flows through our measurement IPs. Approve a 6% signing credit at the ACV threshold of $420k ARR. If Vertex pushes for a deeper signing concession, we should trade for a firm onboarding date and a short-term add-on purchase schedule (months 4 and 7 at minimum volumes).

Markus — legal is likely to push back on the egress attribution clause ("designated IP ranges"). Any alternative language you'd prefer to keep the credit but reduce operational friction?

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-26T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring price parity + migration credits (legal redline suggestion)

Team —

Suggested compromise for procurement: replace hard requirement to route through "designated IP ranges" with an attribution clause that allows either designated IP ranges OR signed traffic manifests + shared CDN logs for the migration window. This gives Vertex flexibility if they have managed networking constraints while preserving our ability to validate credits. We'll append an audit right limited to migration windows and anonymized transfer-level reporting.

I also redlined language on termination: credits applied in months 1-3 are refundable as an offset if Vertex terminates within 90 days of go-live only if the termination is for cause. That prevents misuse of the migration credit during POC churn.

Markus Klein
Head of Commercial Legal
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline-terms-20270426.docx
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Caldwell <alex.caldwell@vertexsys.com>, procure@vertexsys.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-27T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: Phased egress credits + tiered seat bundles (final)

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a final commercial proposal (v2) and a short egress-example workbook showing how credits would apply across a 3-month migration. Highlights:
- Egress credit schedule: 90% month 1 / 60% month 2 / 30% month 3 (applies to validated migration transfer as per the mutually agreed attribution method).
- Tiered seat bundles: Starter (up to 25 seats), Growth (26-150 seats), Scale (151+). Vertex can execute incremental seat purchases at months 4 & 7 at a 12% discount to list for those tranches if bundled in the 12-month commitment.
- Signing credit: 6% one-time credit at $420k ARR commitment.
- Legal: agreed compromise on attribution (IP ranges OR signed manifests + CDN logs). Audit right limited to migration windows; termination refund guardrails included in redline.

If procurement agrees, we can run DocuSign this week and schedule a short kickoff with PS. I'll also open a HubSpot task and send a DocuSign link once you confirm.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270427_vertex-proposal-v2.pdf, egress-credit-examples.xlsx, redline-terms-20270426.docx
